item.title: Architecture Decisions for Marin 535B-A23B
item.description: The goals, experiments, and judgment calls behind the architecture of Marin 535B-A23B, from model sizing and EP token dropping to each notable component.
item.author: Larry Dial

item.title: Scaling Marin's Open LLM Pre-Training
item.description: At Open Athena's first community meetup, Will Held walked us through Marin's pre-training process, particularly the hero training run, which wrapped up this week.
item.author: Will Held

item.title: Post-Training in the Open
item.description: We’re excited to share more about our progress post-training our mixture of experts models. Our latest milestone is the release of Marin 67B-A2B “Snowball” v0.1, a mixture of experts model trained on ten trillion tokens. We’ve built a fully open post-training stack, code, and data, and post-trained a model to GPT-OSS-level quality, putting Snowball nine to fifteen months behind the open-weights frontier for similarly sized models.
item.author: Ben Feuer

item.title: There is no posttraining data commons
item.description: The LLM revolution ran on a pretraining commons that humanity built for other reasons. Posttraining consumes tasks, not documents, and no such commons exists. If the open models community wants one, it will have to be built deliberately.
item.author: David Hall

item.title: Meet our team: Tim O'Donnell
item.description: In this Q&A, Tim O’Donnell reveals his most memorable AI turning point, explains how Open Athena acts as a “third place,” and shares his favorite town for peaceful bike rides.

item.title: Expert parallelism at hero scale
item.description: Expert Parallelism made a 535B-A23B model practical to train. We compare FSDP, fixed-capacity EP, and results from a scaling ladder.

item.description: How MarinDNA combined data curation, hyperparameter transfer, scaling, and data-mixture experiments to build an efficient 1B alignment-free genomic language model with balanced performance across genomic regions.

item.title: Scaling Samudra: Our journey towards better ocean emulators
item.description: We scaled Samudra, our neural ocean emulator, to train on 16x more data on the same hardware — cutting training time from four days to four hours. We found out systems performance tuning is a humbling process.

item.title: I argued with the father of open source for 2 years. Now the AI fight is the same — only bigger.

item.title: Research Software Engineering in the Age of Agentic Tooling
item.description: With the rise of AI coding agents, the role of research software engineers is changing. Instead of building libraries and using them to write bespoke code, RSEs must shift their focus both upstream and downstream of the software creation process.
item.author: Yael Elmatad

item.title: Meet our team: Betsy Cannon

item.title: Open Development of Frontier AI
item.description: Open development is key to making frontier-level artificial intelligence legible, reusable, and public.

item.title: Cluster Scheduling with Iris
item.description: Training a frontier-level LLM requires significant resources across a variety of providers and accelerator types. Our Iris scheduling system has allowed us to effectively make use of these precious resources using a custom global scheduler; in the months since rollout, our sustained concurrent TPU usage has roughly doubled.
item.author: Russell Power

item.title: Preparing for the AI Future with Ethics in Mind
item.description: At a recent panel discussion, our COO and CSO Jared Crooks explained why openness is key to understanding AI, and dug into the importance of embedding ethics in this new technology.
item.author: Jared Crooks

item.title: Improving our LLM Pretraining Efficiency
item.description: How Marin pretraining became more efficient through Mixture of Experts, higher expert sparsity, MuonH, PKO, and routed expert normalization.
item.author: Larry Dial

item.title: Scaling Laws That Extrapolate 300× Past the Fit
item.description: Delphi is an open scaling suite ranging from 3e18 to 1e23 FLOPs. A pre-registered forecast from its scaling law predicted the loss of the largest run within 0.2%, extrapolating 300× past the largest run used in the fit.
item.author: Will Held

item.title: Mixture of Experts Quantile Balancing: Validated at 32B-A5B (1e22 FLOPs) Scale
item.description: Quantile Balancing (QB) is a hyperparameter-free load balancer for Mixture of Experts models, introduced by Jianlin Su. We validated it on a 32B-A5B (1e22 FLOPs) Marin run over 326B tokens: zero hyperparameters, zero loss spikes, and no need for leading dense layers, auxiliary losses, or capacity overload factors.
item.author: Larry Dial

item.title: Problems with Chinchilla Approach 2
item.description: The Chinchilla paper's "Approach 2," fitting parabolas to IsoFLOP curves, turns out to have some subtle biases that can add up. We show these can lead to non-trivial errors in compute-optimal allocation (around 6.5% of total compute for Llama 3, worth over $1M in GPU time), especially when IsoFLOP grids aren't perfectly centered or symmetric. The paper also proposes a reparameterization of "Approach 3" that makes direct parametric fitting simple and stable. You can even run it in 70 lines of JavaScript.
item.author: Eric Czech
